Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. d2: The binding asks only whether the object remains a DVD, so it rewards recognizable disc shape and misses whether the requested edit was actually applied to the source DVD. In the images, the source DVD is the small square case near the center; the black object to its right appears to be a separate animal, not the DVD. The edited image removes the case and shows two white discs, while the animal remains. Refine this node’s binding/criterion to compare the source DVD’s location and identity across snapshots and assess the requested transformation on that object, rather than treating any nearby white disc as proof of success. Preserve an unresolved outcome when correspondence is uncertain; do not infer completion from color or shape alone. The five consistent high-confidence passes indicate a systematic binding/evidence error, not transport or dependency failure. The aggregate ‘no’ is a constraint on the overall edit judgment, not atomic ground truth for this identity check.
d1: The binding must track the specific source DVD, not merely detect a white disc in the edited image. The source DVD is the small square case near the center; the black shape to its right is a separate animal. In the edited image the case is gone and two white discs appear, so the repeated high-confidence passes likely mistake a new or unrelated disc for the transformed DVD. Refine the binding and criterion to compare the source object’s identity and location across snapshots, and judge whether that object was transformed; cite the correspondence evidence. Keep the result unresolved if identity cannot be established rather than treating color alone as proof. The repeated passes indicate a systematic visual-binding error, not a transport or dependency failure. Use the aggregate “no” only as a constraint on the overall edit judgment, not as atomic ground truth for this node.
